reason: 'blocked on the thrust stage in the main house, with the audience in a single dark wedge facing the action' / 'composing for a single viewpoint'. A thrust stage has the audience on three sides (Wikipedia, Thrust stage); a single facing audience describes a proscenium stage.

'She ran the letters again from the beginning. Serine, histidine, glycine, leucine.' Read from the first letter, UCC AUG GGA CUU decodes as serine, methionine, glycine, leucine; there is no CAU (histidine) or GGG codon in that frame.

'the red of the lower half and the blood at the corners of her mouth' / 'the corset is grey because her actual corset was grey'. In The Broken Column her lower body is wrapped in a white sheet, the corset straps are white, and there is no blood at her mouth, only tears (NYU Medical Humanities, medhum.med.nyu.edu/view/12902).

'a single person deciding, on a Thursday in March, to walk through a particular door and press a particular button.' 28 March 1979 was a Wednesday, and Commons divisions are counted by MPs walking through lobbies, not by pressing buttons.

'two moles of water for every mole of oxygen'. In CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O there is one mole of water per mole of O2 (5.0 g O2 = 0.156 mol gives 0.156 mol H2O). Also 'how many sandwiches... Two... Right.': two slices of bread make one sandwich, so the limiting-reactant analogy is miscounted.

'Fourteen names had NULL beside them, and at the top... was Mr. Halloran.' Halloran has an order (the 1998 plum tree), so a Customers LEFT JOIN Orders returns that order row for him, not NULL; NULL only appears for customers with no orders at all.

uncertain: 'the flowers hot pinks and reds' in Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird; sources (Wikipedia) describe leaves, butterfly clips and dragonflies but no flowers, and the monkey tugs the thorn necklace rather than a ribbon.
'Isabelle marries Heathcliff to escape her brother's control'. The character in Wuthering Heights is Isabella Linton, not Isabelle.

'the aluminum frame that had been bent so many times by deliveries that it had gone ductile, soft at the corner'. Repeated bending work-hardens and fatigues aluminum, making it less ductile, not more.
